extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys, patent examiners, and legal practitioners dealing with patents in the Russian Federation
extracted.subtask_description: Rules, substantive standards, and procedural requirements for obtaining, maintaining, enforcing and challenging patents, useful model certificates and industrial design patents under the Patent Law of the Russian Federation (1992, as amended).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability requirements for inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention is patentable if it is novel, possesses an inventive level, and is industrially applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Novelty = not identifiable on a technological level; inventive level = not evident to a specialist from the technological level; industrial applicability = can be used in industry, agriculture, health service or other sectors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of novelty (inventions)
rubrics_metrics.description: The invention shall be deemed novel if it is not identifiable on a technological level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The technological level includes any information that became universally available before the invention priority date; when establishing novelty, all prior applications and patents (with earlier priority) in the Russian Federation are taken into account (except revoked ones).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of inventive level / non-obviousness
rubrics_metrics.description: The invention shall be deemed to have an inventive level if it is evident to a specialist that the invention does not come from the technological level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluated against the technological level (prior art); expert examination considers whether the formulated invention corresponds to patentability terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of industrial applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention or useful model is industrially applicable if it is able to be used in industry, agriculture, the health service, and other sectors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For industrial designs, industrial applicability means the design may be reproduced repeatedly by manufacture of the corresponding item.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grace period for disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosure by author, applicant or persons who received it directly or indirectly does not defeat patentability if application is filed within six months from disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The duty to prove the fact of disclosure rests with the applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentable subject matter (examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject matter may include a device, method, substance, microorganism strain, plant or animal cell culture, and use of a known item for a new purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are listed as possible subjects of an invention (Article 4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Excluded subject matter (unpatentable inventions)
rubrics_metrics.description: The following are not patentable: scientific theories and mathematical methods; methods of organizing/managing economy; conventional symbols, timetables, regulations; methods of mental operations; algorithms and computer programmes; projects/schemes for structures and territorial layouts; solutions concerning only outer appearance aimed at aesthetics; topologies of integrated microcircuits; plant varieties and animal breeds; and solutions contravening public interest, humanity and morality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These categories are expressly listed in Article 4. Similar exclusions apply to useful models and industrial designs as indicated in later articles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terms of patentability for useful models
rubrics_metrics.description: A useful model is granted protection if it is novel and industrially applicable; novelty assessed by aggregate essential features unknown at the technological level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful models exclude methods, substances, microorganism strains, plant/animal cell cultures and their novel utilization, and items listed as unpatentable in Article 4.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terms of patentability for industrial designs
rubrics_metrics.description: An industrial design is granted protection if it is novel, original and industrially applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Novelty = aggregate essential properties determining aesthetic/ergonomic features unknown from prior universally available information; originality = essential properties determine creative nature of aesthetic features; industrial applicability = may be reproduced repeatedly by manufacture. Exclusions: designs dependent exclusively on technical function; architectural objects (except minor forms); printed matter as such; variable-shape items formed by liquids/gases/non-cohesive materials; items contrary to public interest or morality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope/volume of legal protection
rubrics_metrics.description: The legal protection for inventions/useful models is specified by their formulas (claims); for industrial designs by aggregate substantial properties reflected in product/model/figure photographs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims/formula define scope; for designs the list of essential features and images determine protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent term durations and prolongation limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Invention patent term: 20 years from filing; useful model certificate valid for 5 years from arrival with possibility of extension by no more than 3 years; industrial design patent valid for 10 years from arrival with possibility of extension by no more than 5 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prolongation/prolongation procedures specified by Patent Agency rules and upon request of patent holder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity requirement for applications
rubrics_metrics.description: An application must concern only one invention (or a group of inventions so interconnected as to form a single inventive scheme); similar unity rules apply for useful models and industrial designs (a single design or versions thereof).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unity of invention/useful model/industrial design is required; transformations between application types allowed prior to publication under conditions stated in the Law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal application contents (invention)
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention application must contain: application form indicating author(s) and person(s) in whose name patent is requested; a description disclosing the invention in full sufficient for implementation; the formula (claims) expressing the substance fully based on description; drawings and other materials if necessary; and a summary. Evidence of duty payment or grounds for exemption/reduction must be appended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent Agency establishes detailed document requirements (Rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal application contents (useful model)
rubrics_metrics.description: A useful model application must contain: application indicating author(s) and claimant(s); a description disclosing the model in full sufficient for implementation; useful model formula fully based on description; drawings; and a summary. Evidence of duty payment or grounds for exemption/reduction must be appended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unity requirement applies; Patent Agency specifies detailed requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal application contents (industrial design)
rubrics_metrics.description: An industrial design application must contain: application indicating author(s) and claimant(s); set of pictures reflecting the article/model/figure providing full and detailed idea of external appearance; drawings showing general view, ergonomic scheme, confection chart if necessary; and a description including list of essential properties. Evidence of duty payment or grounds for exemption/reduction must be appended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Versions of the design may be included; Patent Agency specifies detailed requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language and translation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications shall be submitted in the Russian language; other documents may be in another language but a Russian translation must be appended. Translation may be submitted within two months after the application arrived at the Patent Agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foreign applicants or documents in other languages must provide translations within the specified time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation by registered patent attorneys
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications may be submitted through a patent attorney who is registered at the Patent Agency; natural persons and foreign entities shall conduct business through registered patent attorneys to keep business valid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authority of attorney must be certified by a power of attorney; Patent Agency/Regulations set requirements for registration and certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority rules and Paris Convention periods
rubrics_metrics.description: Priority is established from the arrival date at Patent Agency of the application containing request, description, formula and drawings. Convention (Paris) priority: inventions and useful models — 12 months; industrial designs — 6 months. Applicant must indicate use of conventional priority when filing or within two months, and supply copy of initial application not later than three months from arrival.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority may also be established from various earlier filings under specified conditions; rules allow certain extensions for circumstances beyond applicant's control (not more than two months).

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of application documents by applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: During two months after receipt of the application the applicant has the right to make corrections and specifications without changing the substance of the invention/useful model/industrial design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If duty paid, corrections and specifications may be submitted in the invention application after this two-month period but not later than ruling on expert examination of merits; corrections changing substance are not allowed (treated as independent application).

rubrics_metrics.name: Official expert examination procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Official expert examination begins after two months from arrival (can be started earlier on written request, but then applicant loses right to make corrections without duty). Examination checks presence of necessary documents, observance of statutory requirements, and whether the suggestion concerns facilities granted legal protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If additional materials were appended under Article 20, the expert checks whether they change the substance. If application corresponds to patentability terms, ruling made to grant patent; otherwise ruling to refuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional materials and timelines during examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Experts may request additional materials necessary for examination (including modified claims); applicant must submit these within two months of receipt of inquiry (or request extension). Failure to submit or extend leads to application deemed revoked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional materials that change the essence/substance of the invention are not taken into consideration and may be filed as independent application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals and third-party participation in examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may object to a refusal within three months; Appeal Chamber examines objections within four months. Disagreement with Appeal Chamber ruling can be appealed to the Supreme Patent Chamber within six months. Third persons may request expert examination within three years after submission of application (otherwise application deemed revoked).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent Agency must notify applicant of third-party requests; Supreme Patent Chamber rulings are final.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporary legal protection from publication
rubrics_metrics.description: A filed invention is given temporary legal protection within the scope of the published claims from date of publication of application information until the date of publication of grant information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If refusal ruling is final, temporary protection does not apply. Persons who used claimed invention during this period shall pay compensation to patent holder after patent grant; amount by agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expert examination regime for useful models
rubrics_metrics.description: During expert examination of a useful model, correspondence to patentability terms (novelty/inventive level) is not verified; a certificate is issued under applicant's responsibility without guarantee of validity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Official examination checks formal correctness and whether suggestion relates to patentable facilities; information retrieval may be requested without specifying level of technology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expert examination regime for industrial designs
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent Agency conducts official expert examination and an expert examination concerning merits for industrial designs; applicable procedural provisions similar to those for inventions (Articles 21 and related items).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Positive result of official examination leads to merits examination; after publication, materials are accessible to any person.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for disputing and invalidating patents
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent may be disputed/invalidated in whole or partly if: (a) the patented object fails to correspond to patentability terms; (b) the claims of an invention/useful model contain aggregate essential features of an industrial design absent in initial materials; (c) authors or patent holders are incorrectly indicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objections on such grounds are examined by Appeal Chamber within six months of arrival; further appeals available to Supreme Patent Chamber.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination of patent before term
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent terminates before appointed time if: it is deemed invalid under Article 29; upon application of patent holder to Patent Agency; or if maintenance duties are not paid within established time-limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent Agency publishes information in official bulletin about early termination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights and duties of the patent holder (exclusive rights)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent holder enjoys the exclusive right to use the patented invention/useful model/industrial design and to prohibit others from using it, subject to rights of other patent holders and exceptions in the Law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If patent belongs to several persons, use/licensing relationships determined by agreement; cession (assignment) of patent must be registered with Patent Agency to be valid. Patents and rights are inheritable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of patent infringement
rubrics_metrics.description: Infringement is unsanctioned manufacture, use, import, offer to sell, sale or other introduction into economic turnover, or storage with such aims, of a product containing the patented invention/useful model/design; and use of a patented method or introduction into turnover of a product directly obtained by a patented method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A product is deemed manufactured using a patented invention/useful model if each respective feature of the invention or equivalent feature has been used; a product made by the patented method is presumed obtained by that method absent evidence to the contrary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actions not deemed infringement (exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Not infringement: use of patented facilities when designing/operating foreign transport temporarily/accidentally present on RF territory (reciprocity required); conduct of research or experiments; use in force majeure with commensurate compensation; personal non-profit use; one-time manufacture of medicines in pharmacies on physician's prescription; use of goods legally introduced into economic turnover.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are explicit statutory exceptions (Article 11) and include conditions in each subitem (e.g., reciprocity for transport).

rubrics_metrics.name: Right of prior use
rubrics_metrics.description: A person who, prior to the priority date, voluntarily used on RF territory an identical solution developed independently, or made preparations therefor, retains the right to further use it free of charge without expanding its scope of use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Right of prior use may be transferred only jointly with the production in which the identical solution was used or preparation was made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compulsory (non-exclusive) license for non-use or insufficient use
rubrics_metrics.description: If the patent holder does not use or insufficiently uses an invention or industrial design for four years from issue (three years for a useful model), and refuses to grant a license, any person desiring and ready to use it may apply to the Supreme Patent Chamber requesting a compulsory non-exclusive license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supreme Patent Chamber grants license if patent holder cannot prove valid excuses; it specifies extent of use, size, terms and order of payments. License payments established not below market price.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to demand license when mutual blocking of rights
rubrics_metrics.description: If the patent holder cannot use an invention/useful model/industrial design without infringing another patent holder's rights, he may demand that the latter conclude a license contract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This facilitates cross-licensing where rights overlap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment and license registration requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Cession (assignment) and license contracts must be registered with the Patent Agency; without registration the contract is deemed invalid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules for consideration and registration are specified by Patent Agency decisions; parties must follow registration formalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open license and reduced duty
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent holder may file application to allow him to grant to any person the right to use an object (open license); in that case duty for keeping the patent in force shall be reduced by 50% from the year following the year in which information about the application was published. Application for open license is irrevocable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Persons expressing desire to use shall conclude payment contracts; disputes considered by Supreme Patent Chamber.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government use for national security
rubrics_metrics.description: In the interests of national security the Government may allow use of a patented object without patent holder's consent, with payment of commensurate compensation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disputes over amount of compensation resolved by Supreme Patent Chamber.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication content and access to application materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon granting, Patent Agency publishes information including author name (if agreed), patent holder, name and formula of invention/useful model, or list of essential features and image of industrial design. After publication any person may familiarize with application materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent Agency determines full composition of published information; applicants may request earlier publication; author may refuse to be mentioned as such in published information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration in state registers and patent issuance
rubrics_metrics.description: Simultaneously with publication of grant information Patent Agency enters corresponding object in State Register of Inventions/Useful Models/Industrial Designs and issues the patent to person in whose name it was claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If several persons claimed the patent in their names, a single patent is issued to them all; Patent Agency specifies patent form and composition of information; corrections of obvious and technical errors may be entered on demand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revocation and transformation of applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may revoke application prior to publication (but not later than registration of industrial design or useful model). Prior to publication of information on invention application, applicant may transform it into an application for a useful model (and vice versa before ruling issuing certificate). Priority of initial application remains valid after transformation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transformation procedures and timing are regulated by Law (Article 28).

rubrics_metrics.name: Time-limit restoration
rubrics_metrics.description: Time-limits (except certain specified ones) missed by the applicant may be restored by the Patent Agency if applicant corroborates valid excuses and pays the duty; request to restore must be filed no later than twelve months after expiry of missed time-limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Items 7 and 9 of Article 21 excluded from restoration; Patent Agency applies rules consistently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information retrieval services and access to prior art information
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant and third persons may request informational retrieval to specify level of technology for assessing novelty/inventive level; Patent Agency specifies procedure and presentation of retrieval information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After publication any person can access application materials; Patent Agency sends requested patent materials within one month of receipt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compensation and employer-employee rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent shall be granted to author(s) or to natural/legal persons indicated by author or to employer in cases where invention was developed in connection with official duties or specific assignment and contract does not provide otherwise. The author has right to compensation proportionate to profit obtained by employer or possibly obtained as result of use, in cases where employer obtained patent or keeps object secret or fails to obtain patent for employer reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If employer fails to file within four months of notification by author of newly-developed object, author can file and receive patent in own name; disputes on compensation considered by court; other relationships regulated by legislation regarding official inventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liability for violations of authors' rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Appropriation of authorship, compulsion to co-authorship, and illegal disclosure of information concerning an industrial property object entail criminal liability under Russian legislation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criminal responsibility provisions referenced in Article 32; civil remedies also available for infringement (compensation for losses per civil law).
